item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-20
item.description: Two documents, one from Seattle and one from Menlo Park, settle this week what a week of Chinese industry conferences could only assert. On 2026-09-18 Amazon put Kimi K3 on Bedrock; on 2026-11-05 Microsoft put Kimi K3.1 Pro on Foundry; Reuters reported on 2026-08-26 that Moonshot was seeking up to 30 per cent of the revenue those clouds earn from the model, and the K3 licence's USD 20 million MaaS threshold is what makes that ask collectable. Menlo Ventures' 2026 State of Enterprise AI, published 2026-11-03, supplies the number underneath: Chinese models took 89 per cent of global enterprise open-source spend, Kimi alone 61 per cent, while open source overall holds 19 per cent of tokens and 4 per cent of dollars because its average token price fell 3.3 times to USD 0.13. In Shanghai, the same fortnight, the city that wrote a 2027 open-source plan — 1 to 2 globally influential communities, 100 commercialising enterprises, 200 projects, 3 million developers, up to CNY 20 million for foundational tooling — welcomed OSChina's headquarters and its Model Ark Base to Zhangjiang on 2026-10-30, with its CEO describing the city as the place that has both industrial scene density and institutional supply. One city is paying for a distribution layer. One company is taxing a distribution layer. Neither is building a governance body, because a distribution layer does not need one.
